source.title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE
source.authors: Yi Shi; Tan-Yu Chen; Kai Shen

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the localization aspect of V5 by applying directional ablation and comparing writer groups and low-rank subspaces on a frontier MoE model. It does not test the fine-tuning or token-depth claims in the cited original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests directional ablation and refusal outcomes, including which writer groups and ranks are involved. It does not test fine-tuning on harmful or benign data, per-token KL concentration, prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, or safety-deepening training. Cited findings about those topics are background, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study removes a single rank-one refusal direction from every residual writer of a 320B MoE model. It reports harmful-prompt refusal rates before and after removal, broken down by writer group, content category and subspace rank (1–12). These results bear directly on V5's claim that a few ranks or weights carry safety behaviour. There is no fine-tuning, per-token KL, prefilling or deepening training, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 are only cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. A single difference-of-means direction removes 41–89 points of refusal across seven benchmarks with no detected capability change, but only when projected out of all writer groups at once. The authors stress that the non-additivity describes the intervention, not where refusal lives. A category-concentrated residue (violence, sexual content, hate) survives every subspace tested up to rank 12. Scope is one model, one layer, and the procedures tested.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes its core procedure as the unmodified single-direction ablation recipe: difference-of-means direction and rank-one projection. It adds structural enumeration of fused MoE writers, multi-stream activation handling, and iterative block-FP8 requantization. It is not a fine-tuning or response-token-depth experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies by writer-group combination, content category, and subspace rank. The authors report non-monotonic layer effectiveness and select layer 22; judge choice also changes some scores and significance judgments. Rank-sweep subspaces were independently fitted rather than nested.
record.problems: One model and no cross-vendor comparison; no human refusal annotations; only one random orthogonal direction control; rank-sweep subspaces were independently fitted with randomized SVD and no fixed per-call seed; some rank conditions have unfinished or missing responses; capability tests cover sampled subsets and have no power analysis. The authors also state that the editing implementation is withheld, so independent verification requires reimplementation.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 5 clean-variant refusal rows, the XSTest false-refusal result, capability benchmark rows, the Table 8 rule-classifier measurements, and most Table 10 rule-classifier rank rows. Table 10 rule rows for ranks 3 and 8 were retained because the rule classifier's minimum differs from the judge's. Also omitted layer-selection and activation-mask sweeps (§4.2), FP8 requantization/leakage measurements (§4.4), and capability results (§5.1/Table 6), which do not directly measure V5.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.

Individual neuron or parameter localization; other models or vendors; nested-rank effects (subspaces were fitted independently per rank); whether more than one random control direction also does nothing.
No test of data or objective as the cause.

missing.what: Comparison of editing the writers versus projecting at the layer boundary over the same layers: 0.174 vs 0.265 refusal on 253 paired prompts (27 of 31 discordant pairs favour writers, p=3e-5). This bears on where the low-rank edit must be applied.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label on the random-direction controls inverts their meaning: they are specificity controls that support V5, and that label is replaced. The rank-one edit touches all 12,479 writer matrices, so it supports localization in rank, not in a small set of weights. Control rows R01, R09, R17, R22 and R39 are baselines and correctly cannot_determine. Clean-variant, capability, XSTest and Table 8 rule rows are declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of compliance after such fine-tuning.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data.
No per-token KL measurement or analysis of aligned-versus-base output distributions by response position.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test.
Tests writer-group combinations and ranks of 1–12, but not individual-parameter localization, other models, or whether the surviving refusal has a particular mechanism.
Does not test whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
Does not train a method intended to deepen safety or test its persistence.

relationships.condition: Rank-one direction projected out of all residual writers (hooked or baked), general harmful benchmarks
relationships.reason: Refusal falls from 0.92–0.99 to 0.08–0.32 on most benchmarks (R08, R16, R18, R23, R54–R57, R60), while a random orthogonal direction leaves refusal unchanged (R19, R24), so the effect is specific to one low-rank direction.
relationships.display_finding: Refusal fell from 0.92–0.99 to 0.08–0.32 on most benchmarks, while a random orthogonal direction left refusal unchanged.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Rank-one direction projected out of all residual writers (hooked or baked), general harmful benchmarks
source_check.reason: R08, R16, R18, R23 and R54–R57 show large reductions under the targeted direction; R19 and R24 show no comparable reduction under the one random orthogonal control. R60 also shows a substantial reduction from its lower baseline.

relationships.condition: Edits restricted to single writer groups or pairs (weight-group localization)
relationships.reason: No single weight group carries refusal. Attention, dense and expert groups alone remove 0.039, 0.016 (not significant) and 0.148, while 74% of the joint 0.776 effect appears only when all three are edited (R02–R08, R10–R16).
relationships.display_finding: Editing attention, dense or expert groups alone removed 0.039, 0.016 (not significant) and 0.148 of refusal, while 74% of the joint 0.776 effect appeared only when all three were edited.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Edits restricted to single writer groups or pairs (weight-group localization)
source_check.reason: R02–R07 and R10–R15 show dependence on writer-group coverage, with the largest reduction requiring all groups. This qualifies intervention locality; it does not establish where refusal is represented. R11's Rule-specific absent state is unsupported.

relationships.condition: Violence, sexual-content, hate and self-harm-heavy content after the full edit, and category-fitted subspaces of rank 1–12
relationships.reason: Residual refusal stays at 0.38–0.62 in resistant categories and on StrongREJECT and SimpleSafetyTests (R27–R30, R58, R59). Category-fitted subspaces at every rank leave 0.20–0.47 refusal (R40–R53), so low rank does not capture all of the refusal.
relationships.display_finding: Residual refusal stayed at 0.38–0.62 in resistant categories and on StrongREJECT and SimpleSafetyTests. Category-fitted subspaces at every rank still left 0.20–0.47 refusal.

relation.reason: Its own interventions and before/after refusal measurements directly test V5.

tranche.reason: The paper explicitly retains the existing difference-of-means estimator and rank-one ablation recipe, testing it in a new frontier-scale MoE, multi-stream, quantized setting. Structural enumeration and quantization handling adapt its application rather than introduce a different causal method.

source_check.notes: One checkpoint and one random orthogonal control were tested. Rank-sweep subspaces were independently fitted, and increasing unfinished responses complicates interpretation of higher-rank refusal reductions.

statements.correction: GLM-5.3-Flash: 320B total parameters; substantial all-writer refusal reductions; random orthogonal control; capability comparisons and uncertainty reported. Editing implementation, fitted direction, category-fitted subspaces and fitting prompt slices withheld (§6; Limitations).
statements.problem: The numerical summary and controls are supported, but the blanket code-release assertion does not hold for this single-direction study.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Rank-one refusal-direction removal across all writer groups; tested harmful prompts
reader_labels.reason: Rank-one removal substantially lowers refusal on the tested prompts, including the all-writer result and the StrongREJECT and JailbreakBench direction-specific tests (R08, R18, R23, R54–R60). This supports a low-rank component, not localization to a small set of individual weights.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Writer-group subsets and violence-, sexual-content-, and hate-focused subspaces
reader_labels.reason: Single writer groups have much smaller effects than their joint edit, and refusal remains measurable across every tested rank from 1 to 12 on the resistant categories (R02–R07, R27–R38, R40–R53).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Random orthogonal direction control on StrongREJECT and JailbreakBench
reader_labels.reason: Removing a random orthogonal direction leaves refusal at or essentially at the unedited rate, so removal is not explained by projecting out any arbitrary direction (R19, R24).
